### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via SeedSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4e4dfbf9e4acaf3f3f65ce35c71b7a99949cefd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `af9eefa3099b466bb5d3bfd9d38d922320ac0137` — the merge of head `df003ebc97b5b2cc2813688de6e045da9f96c7fb` into base `d4e4dfbf9e4acaf3f3f65ce35c71b7a99949cefd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin af9eefa3099b466bb5d3bfd9d38d922320ac0137 && git checkout af9eefa3099b466bb5d3bfd9d38d922320ac0137
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4e4dfbf9e4acaf3f3f65ce35c71b7a99949cefd df003ebc97b5b2cc2813688de6e045da9f96c7fb && git checkout -B drift-repro d4e4dfbf9e4acaf3f3f65ce35c71b7a99949cefd && git merge --no-ff df003ebc97b5b2cc2813688de6e045da9f96c7fb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4e4dfbf9e4acaf3f3f65ce35c71b7a99949cefd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d4e4dfbf9e4acaf3f3f65ce35c71b7a99949cefd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `45afc37fd3da3dd5998cec64288babd7c34cff4c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts + packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-landed-keys.test.ts, packages/cli/test/package-install-local-sample-owner.integration.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts
Security-touching: no

### ① Derived judgments

- Face: schema. `packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts` changes the `SeedSchema.mode` JSDoc and `.describe()` text only; no key, enum member, default or export moves. The four reference pages under `content/docs/references/` are its regenerated output and carry the same sentence.
- Diff read against merge base `a121e29c280a` (12 files, +522/-38). Check-runs on this head, latest per name: 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure.
- The implementing change is one argument: `runInlineSeed` takes a required `landedKeys: 'honour' | 'reseed'` and hands it to `SeedLoaderService`. Four callers at head: the restart heal (`maybeHealSampleData`, `'honour'`), the fallback `seed-replayer` (`'honour'`, `{ reseed: true }` gives `'reseed'`), `seedUnmanagedCopy` (install `'honour'`, reseed `'reseed'`), `applySideEffects` (install and upgrade `'honour'`, door `reseed` gives `'reseed'`). The three other `SeedLoaderService` constructions in the plugin build the dependency graph only and load nothing.
- `os package install` reaches this same door, so the spec's parenthesis (`os package install`, the marketplace install) names one code path.
- The loads that still keep no record are the seed publish doors (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:5089`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts:107`), which matches "a seed publish keeps no record".
- Security-touching is `no`: no hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential or authentication behaviour. Ownership stamping (#30324) is untouched.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` holds. No accepted shape widens and no public export is added. The loader consults the record only for `upsert` and `ignore` datasets (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts:1564` at head), so an `insert` or `replace` dataset writes exactly what it wrote before and `update` still inserts nothing. No install, upgrade or reseed request moves from served to refused; the `seeded` summary and the reseed answer keep their fields, and a withheld row is counted in the existing `skipped`.
- The fallback `seed-replayer` now reads `options.reseed`. That is the shape the AppPlugin replayer already serves (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:2022`), so the fallback is brought to the existing service shape, not past it.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` accepted: what an author can write is unchanged, and the loader's meaning of each `mode` value is unchanged; which doors keep the record is runtime behaviour.
- `@objectstack/spec` patch (prose only) and `@objectstack/cloud-connection` patch (a fix inside an existing option) are the right levels.
- One served answer does move, outside the Clause-② limbs: the restart's seed outcome goes from settled to failed in a state the PR declares intended. That is M1 in ④.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev question, report 6923758862 (1) and report 6924505372: should the restart heal honour the record. Seat route A (17:24Z, confirmed 17:56Z) answered yes. Read against the tree: route A does change a served outcome. On main a single-tenant restart over a seed a person emptied by hand, not purged, refilled it; main's heal JSDoc lists "never explicitly purged" as the one wanted emptiness, and #30324's own setup comment said so ("not a purge, which would tell the heal the emptiness is wanted"). At head that restart leaves the tables empty. The card's Target names install, upgrade, the per-org replayer and reseed, and the batch ruling 6919107678 described the card to the maintainer as "reinstall, upgrade or reseed"; the restart is in neither. Ruling 6670861426 was read in full and is ownership only ("Every seeding door gets an owner: install, reseed, the rehydrate heal and the per-org replayer"), so changing #30324's setup between its boots breaks no ruling, and its assertions are verbatim in the diff. Route A is consistent with the card's business reason and with the boot seed's rule (#31021). Even so, it reverses a pinned served outcome on a door outside the card and publishes it in `@objectstack/spec` ("with its restart heal"). **Escalated:** this needs the maintainer's word on a decision card, or the heal goes back to the card's named doors. It is not settled by this record.
- Dev question, report 6923758862 (2): prose outside the claimed surface kept in this PR. Answered: keeping it is right. Shipping the door change under a spec description that says a package install keeps no record would publish a false sentence; claim amendments 6923817987 and 6925388752 match the diff.
- Dev out-of-scope notes (no `getFieldFiles` on this door; the loader's `info` line names `seed-replayer` as the way back): neither is in the diff; both stand as notes. The second is N3 below because the spec now names the sample-data reseed as this door's route.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation or in-app join in the product diff. The by-id deletes are in test doubles and test setup only.
- Round 3 report 6925325019 has no open question.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/seed.zod.ts`, sentence by sentence against the tree at this head:

- "the package install or upgrade (`os package install`, the marketplace install) ... record, per organization ... and do not insert again a recorded row that is now gone": holds for `applySideEffects` (the caller's active organization under a wall, otherwise the loader's sole-organization fallback) and for an unmanaged copy's first load.
- "with its restart heal": holds for the rows (heal passes `'honour'`), not for what the restart reports (M1).
- "A key never recorded still lands": holds, loader rule, pinned by the upgrade case.
- "A seed publish keeps no record": holds, see ①.
- "The deliberate re-seed ... or the installed package's sample-data reseed": holds for the ledgered reseed and the unmanaged copy's reseed.
- `.describe()` on each `mode`: `ignore`, `upsert`, `update`, `insert`, `replace` sentences are unchanged and still true; the new clause covers `ignore` and `upsert` only, which is what the loader does.

Break attempts:

- A row deleted after install, then reinstall or upgrade: stays deleted, counted in `skipped`; the reseed brings it back and records it again. Holds.
- The same row, then a restart with every seeded object empty: rows stay deleted, and the boot reports a failed seed. M1.
- A seed row with no stable key (an empty `externalId` component): never recorded, never withheld; unchanged.
- Two packages seeding one object under the same key: the record is keyed by organization, object and key, with no package part, so package B's row is withheld once a person deleted package A's row of that key. This is the loader's existing rule on the boot seed (#31021), now reachable on install; noted, no finding.
- An environment with no `sys_seed_landed_key` rows from before this version: S1.

Findings:

M1 (must-fix) — `maybeHealSampleData` reports the intended honour outcome as a failed heal on every restart. At head (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, the call near line 1988 and the `else` branch near 2008-2022) the result handling is main's: `landed = inserted + updated`, and `landed === 0` logs `warn` "sample-data heal ... landed no rows" and records `{ emptyInstall: true, skipped: 0 }`. With `'honour'`, a restart over a seed a person emptied, or after purge then reinstall (the reinstall clears `sampleDataPurged` on its all-skipped run), withholds every row, so that branch is now the healthy path, taken on every single-tenant boot from then on. `emptyInstall` is read as a failure by the boot banner (`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts:1847`, "installed but 0 rows ⚠"), the `objectstack:seed-settled` message (`packages/cli/src/utils/seed-settled-message.ts:22`, `ok: false`), `GET /ready` where a seed pipeline is registered (`packages/runtime/src/seed-readiness.ts:62` and `:87`, `seed: 'failed'`) and the verify seed outcome (`packages/verify/src/seed-outcome.ts:236-243`, "the boot did not load the seed the app declares"). On main the same restart refilled the rows and answered settled. The loader itself logs this outcome at `info` because it is declared and repeats on every healthy replay. Both new restart pins assert rows only; neither reads the summary or the logger. Fix shape: the heal tells withheld rows (`skipped` above zero, no errors) from a load that landed nothing, reports the first at `info` with the real `skipped` and no `emptyInstall`, and a pin reads the recorded summary in both states. Read from the code, not run.

S1 (should-fix) — "comes back once" understates the window on this door. The changeset ("Rows a person deleted before this release come back once, on the first load after the upgrade") and `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` ("A row deleted before your runtime had this rule comes back once, on the first replay after the upgrade") are true for the boot seed, which loads on every restart and so records every present row at the first boot. Install-local loads nothing at a restart while any seeded row survives (rehydrate calls `applySideEffects` with `seedNow: false`; the heal runs only on full emptiness), so an existing install has no record until its next install, upgrade, reseed or replay. A row a person deletes after this release and before that load still comes back on the next upgrade. Say so in both places, or record the present keys at rehydrate.

N1 (nit) — the install clause lost the organization qualifier the AppPlugin clause keeps. A load with no `config.organizationId` and no sole organization keeps no record (`seed-loader.ts:4712` at head); `seed-data.mdx` says this, the `mode` JSDoc and `.describe()` do not. The JSDoc also lists the `seed-replayer` replay under AppPlugin alone, while this door's fallback replayer now honours the record too.

N2 (nit) — the JSDoc of `maybeHealSampleData` still lists its conditions as on main and does not say a recorded key is withheld; only the inline comment at the call does. `sys-seed-landed-key.object.ts` changes JSDoc on a released package with no changeset line for `@objectstack/platform-objects`; Check Changeset is green on this head, so this is a note.

N3 (nit) — on this door the loader's withheld-rows `info` line still names `seed-replayer` with `{ reseed: true }` as the way back, while the spec text now names the sample-data reseed. The dev noted it; a follow-up card would carry it.

The landed-key suite (15 cases, flat and composed) and the amended #30324 setup agree with the row behaviour the spec text states. The escalation in ③ stands apart from M1: M1 is a defect under route A, and would not exist under the pre-PR heal.
